Q: Simple secure websocket (wss) chat using Node.js server and Jquery client A:

Yes, WSS can work without mod_proxy_wstunnel.

In your setup, the browser connects directly to the Node.js HTTPS/WebSocket server:

new WebSocket("wss://example.com:8089");

So Apache is not involved in the WebSocket connection.

You only need Apache WebSocket proxying when the connection goes through Apache, for example:

Browser → Apache → Node.js

Also, avoid inserting messages using .html() or raw string concatenation because it can cause XSS. Use .text() or textContent instead.

Q: Fatal error: Call to undefined method CI_Session::sess_destroy() 1.7.2 A:

When you are trying to destroy the session also, you have to load $this->load->library('session');

That should be the reason,

So load session library automatically, It's more convenient rather than calling $this->load->library('session') every where.

It's in application/config/autoload.php

Q: Dropdown menu not working in IE6 or IE7 works fine in Firefox A:

Try setting a doctype. I know I've had issues in the past with hover events without a correct doctype. Your current page sets Internet Explorer to Quirks Mode.

Currently if, in IE9 I set my mode to IE7 and then switch the "Document Mode" from "Quirks Mode" to "Internet Explorer 7" mode, they show up correctly.

Put this at the top of your HTML files and see if setting your doctype will fix the issue:

<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//EN"
   "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/loose.dtd">

Q: Import Google Fonts with scss: MIME-Type Conflict A:

I think the key, as noted by the previous poster, is that if you're getting this MIME type mismatch in your browser console, and particularly if it's returning "text/html", then there was probably an error. Try taking the URL and putting it into a separate browser tab and see what you get back.

I was running into the same issue, and it was only when I did this that I discovered this:

400: Invalid selector

icon names must be sorted alphabetically

Granted, this is in the documentation, but it's easy to miss (as I obviously did).

Q: Implementing a custom comparer that treats the numbers as integers rather than strings A:

Microsoft sorts numbers as text by default

No it doesn't, and your code doesn't show anything different. Disproving this is easy as this C# fiddle and this DB fiddle show:

var numbers=  new List<int> { 1, 11, 2, 3, 10 };
numbers.Sort();
Console.WriteLine(String.Join(",",numbers));
-----
1,2,3,10,11

create table Numbers(num int);
insert into Numbers
values (1), (11), (2), (3), (10);

select * from Numbers order by num;
-----
1
2
3
10
11

All database applications (in any language) depend on numbers getting sorted as numbers, so if what you claims were true, everyone would notice. You'll have to provide actual code, the actual table schema and actual data so others can replicate this extraordinary claim.

Chances are that the application itself stores numbers as strings, which is an application bug. Perhaps you're actually storing a week number as string?

Or perhaps you didn't use an ORDER BY clause? Table rows have no inherent order. The database (any database, not just SQL Server) will return rows in the cheapest way if you don't use an ORDER BY clause.

You didn't post your table or any query that compares anything, so it's impossible to guess what's going on.

Q: Need help with MySql query A:

If you want to delete users where any of the records for that user has tonetone as a meta_value, you can do this:

CREATE TABLE wp_usermeta_users_to_delete
( user_id BIGINT(20) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY );
INSERT INTO wp_usermeta_users_to_delete
SELECT DISTINCT user_id FROM wp_usermeta
WHERE meta_value = "tonetone";
DELETE A. FROM wp_usermeta A INNER JOIN wp_usermeta_users_to_delete B USING (user_id);
DROP TABLE wp_usermeta_users_to_delete;*
